why:
ABSORBED at 5.1.0. The previous record was 45/0: the launch set had been redefined from `tier === "core"` to `effectiveTier !== "quarantine"`, which moved the governed count from 0 to 45 while 45 rules were already shipping in every default report. That redefinition was declared with an ANTI-CREEP-EXCEPTION in the 5.1.0 entry and shipped in af00a5ae.

`previousBaselineCore` stays 0 rather than becoming 45 on purpose: the law compares the tier against the PREVIOUS baseline, so leaving it at 0 makes the move from 0 to 45 visible as growth of 45. Lowering it to 45 in the same edit would make the redefinition of the governed set look like a legal no-op, which is the exact escape the comparison-against-previous rule exists to close.
howToMove: Set previousBaselineCore to the value you are replacing whenever you record a new baselineCore. The law compares the tier against previousBaselineCore, so lowering baselineCore to match a grown tier does NOT hide the growth. A tier bigger than previousBaselineCore needs an ANTI-CREEP-EXCEPTION line in the CURRENT CHANGELOG entry (the unreleased one if it has content, else the release heading below it); a tier at or under it needs nothing.
